original.target_description: Study 2, reassurance seeking and ACT performance; multiple partial-correlation tests with different covariates on journal p. 276. Description and p. 6 locator do not identify a unique test.

n.sample_role: Participants: 151 survey completers; 148 have reassurance-seeking scores and 150 have ACT scores. These are recruitment/measure counts, not established critical-model analytic N.
n.exclusions: Pairwise deletion for Table 2 correlations, with Ns ranging from 130 to 151; no explicit complete-case N or exclusions for candidate partial-correlation models in the excerpt.

notes: Identity: title and DOI exactly match the neutral original reference. Running header is Knoll et al.; no full author byline is present, so Valentiner/Holzman cannot be independently verified from a byline. Assessment 26(2) journal headers and empirical methods/results/Table 2 are consistent with the assigned primary report. Supplied provenance identifies an author-provided HTML frozen excerpt, journal pp. 274–279; retained lines begin at L715 and end at L1403. It is not the complete paper. No PDF supplied. Target ambiguity: several full-scale reassurance-seeking/ACT partial correlations appear on p. 276: controlling test anxiety, partial r = −.32, p < .001 (respectively mapping follows the text ordering Superstitious Behaviors then Reassurance Seeking); controlling test anxiety, high school ranking percentile, high school GPA, first semester college GPA and depression, partial r = −.35, p < .001; controlling Superstitious Behavior, partial r = −.33, p < .001. Each is a candidate, none selected. Other distinct candidates: Table 2 zero-order r = −.43, **p < .01; follow-up Intest Reassurance Seeking controlling Pretest, partial r = .07, p = .38; Pretest Reassurance Seeking controlling Intest, partial r = −.42, p < .001. No metric converted. N: 151 survey completers, separate measure counts 148 and 150, and pairwise correlation range 130–151 do not establish an analytic N for the target partial-correlation model. The measure counts overlap and cannot be summed. No arithmetic derivation. All assigned values remain null for unresolved evidence/target correspondence. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
